Lumber company raises $4M for pediatric rehabilitation program, earns Everyday Hero Award
November 25, 2026 | 10:48 am CST
Lumber company raises $4M for pediatric rehabilitation program, earns Everyday Hero Award
David Fitch of Fitch Lumber Company is the 2026 winner, leading the Fitch Family Comprehensive Pediatric Rehabilitation Program. Photo by Fitch Lumber.

ECI Software Solutions, Inc., a provider of AI-powered, cloud-based business management software and services, announced the winner of its annual Everyday Hero Award, honoring an ECI customer who raised nearly $4 million for children’s rehabilitation care in North Carolina.
The finalists were celebrated at ECI’s Connect Customer Conference, which took place November 16-18, 2026, at the Cosmopolitan Resort in Las Vegas.

Everyday Hero Award Winner: David Fitch
Now in its 11th year, the Everyday Hero Award program honors ECI customers who consistently go above and beyond to help others and make a difference in their communities. Nominations are submitted by ECI employees, customers, and partners and are evaluated by a panel of judges.

David Fitch of Fitch Lumber Company, a fourth-generation family business in Carrboro, N.C., is the 2026 winner, leading the Fitch Family Comprehensive Pediatric Rehabilitation Program. After his 10-year-old son was seriously injured by a car, the family learned that there was no inpatient pediatric rehabilitation unit nearby. His son had to travel nine hours by ambulance to Atlanta for care.

Fitch and his family have since raised nearly $4 million toward a pediatric rehabilitation program at the North Carolina Children’s Hospital, providing a place for local children to recover closer to home. As the winner, ECI will donate $15,000 to the program in Fitch’s honor.
The 2026 Everyday Hero Award finalists include:
Shane Sullivan, Caruso Homes: Works with Caruso Cares, the company’s employee-led charity that repairs homes for elderly and disabled neighbors in Prince George’s County.
Milli Arakawa, Neighborhoods of EYA: Co-founded the volunteer-run One Desk Foundation in 2010, whose Home Run Heroes program honors outstanding elementary students at Washington Nationals games.
ECI will donate $7,500 to a charity chosen by each finalist.
Visit the Everyday Hero Award page to learn more about the impact these winners and finalists have made on their communities and businesses.
